newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-PARNEVIK GOES THREE SHOTS AHEAD AT OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PARNEVIK GOES THREE SHOTS AHEAD AT OPEN.

text.p: Northern Irishman Darren Clarke fell three shots behind Swedish leader Jesper Parnevik with a double bogey at the second hole in the final round of the British Open at Royal Troon on Sunday.
But Masters champion Tiger Woods failed to get the fast start he needed to put pressure on the leaders as he could only par the first three holes.
He remained eight shots behind Parnevik, who parred the opening hole after hitting his second into a greenside bunker and then parred the second as well.
Clarke drove to the front edge of the 364-yard first green and two-putted from 50 feet for birdie, holing a tricky second effort of seven feet to get within one stroke of Parnevik.
But he struck an iron tee-shot out of bounds on to the beach off the second tee and ran up a six as his two-shot overnight deficit increased to three.
American Justin Leonard birdied the second and third to draw level with Clarke.
Parnevik, wearing purple drainpipe trousers, hit an iron off the first tee and still had 150 yards to go but pulled his second shot into a greenside bunker in a downhill lie.
But he blasted out to 18 inches and holed to save par, then made a routine par at the second.
Woods drove into rough at the first and pulled his second into a greenside bunker, then had to hole a 12-footer to save par.
He two-putted from 40 feet for par at the second and from 12 feet at the third as he remained eight shots off the pace.
American Tom Lehman ended his disappointing title defence on an upbeat note with a five-under-par 66 containing five birdies and no dropped shots.
"I played awfully well last week to win at Loch Lomond but I didn't have my game this week.
"The back nine has kicked me in the butt all week and my two birdies on the back nine today were my first all week," he said.
"It has been a great experience and though I wish I could have played better earlier on, the reception coming up the 18th was fantastic," he said.
Three-times winner Nick Faldo completed what seemed likely to be his worst British Open since he was joint 53rd in 1985.
Faldo, the winner in 1987, 1990 and 1992, compiled a closing 72 after birdies at the last two holes for a total of 291, seven over par.
He was unlikely to make the top 50. "My game was about 10 per cent off this week and that makes a big difference. You have to keep the ball in play and I was not in play the whole time," he said.
Another three-times champion, American Jack Nicklaus, finished with a 75 for 293, nine over par.
